system_config.scenario_scale: Toy projects and undergraduate-level applications (Exclude everything listed in inputs.out_of_scope and enterprise over-engineering)
system_config.technical_depth: Advanced CS undergraduate level (Focus on the internal mechanisms listed in inputs.focus_mechanisms)

task: Design a logical, expository JSON outline that explains everything from core concepts and internal mechanisms to practical application in order to support the given core_argument.
constraints: output_language: Write every string value in English, except core_message, which is copied verbatim from inputs.core_argument.
core_message: Copy the exact string from inputs.core_argument 100% verbatim without any modification or translation.

problem_statement: Strictly forbid first-person anecdotes (e.g., 'When I built...'). Describe a concrete, hypothetical problem situation: the code path that runs and the wrong result that is observed.

no_instruction_terms: Use scenario_scale and technical_depth only to calibrate depth. Never write the project scale, audience level, or wording from these instructions (e.g., 'toy project', 'undergraduate', 'dilemma') into output text.
expository_flow: Do NOT mechanically list 1:1 pros and cons. Instead, explain HOW the mechanisms in inputs.focus_mechanisms operate under the hood.
section_count: deep_dive_sections MUST contain at least 3 sections. Never output fewer than 3 sub_topics.
argument_placement: deep_dive_sections explain why the problem in problem_statement occurs. Do NOT state the core_argument's solution there; state it only in practical_application.

principle_shape: Write principle as exactly two sentences: (1) a topic sentence stating how the mechanism works, which the paragraph will develop, and (2) a concluding sentence stating what necessarily follows from it, independent of the scenario. Name a framework class or method only if the reader will meet it in logs, stack traces, or while debugging.

causal_mechanism: Write mechanism_explanation as one declarative causal sentence following the structure: 'When [A: the code path from the problem situation] executes, due to [B: the principle], [C: the observed result] occurs.'
no_meta_commentary: Strictly forbid meta-statements explaining the purpose of the article (e.g., 'This article explores...', 'Let's take a look at...').
concise_takeaway: Compress key_takeaway into a single English noun phrase of at most 10 words.

problem_statement.description: Concrete hypothetical problem situation: the code path that runs and the wrong result observed (No 1st-person or meta-commentary)

concept_definition.description: Clear definitions of the core concepts named in inputs.topic and their structural roles

deep_dive_sections.description: Expository sections explaining, through internal mechanisms, why the problem in problem_statement occurs; one section per item of inputs.focus_mechanisms

sub_topic.description: Specific CS mechanism topic taken from inputs.focus_mechanisms

principle.description: Exactly two sentences: a topic sentence on how the mechanism works + a concluding sentence on what follows from it (scenario-independent)

mechanism_explanation.description: One causal sentence on what goes wrong in the problem_statement scenario because of this mechanism (Code path A -> Principle B -> Observed result C). Do not restate core_argument.

key_takeaway.description: Single English noun phrase, max 10 words

architecture_pattern.description: Concrete design (schema, code, or configuration) that puts inputs.core_argument into practice and resolves the problem_statement scenario

exception_case.description: Cases where inputs.core_argument does not hold and the opposite choice is acceptable, to prevent dogmatic application
